## What Two Satellites Infer from a Changing Gap

Two satellites follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they approach a larger concentration of mass, stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.

The changing distance between them is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass. The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets, and sea level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
